biography: Marcos Gracia, born in the vibrant heart of São Paulo, Brazil, wasn't raised in the lap of racing luxury. His father, a mechanic, instilled in him a love for engines and speed, but racing seemed a distant dream. It wasn't until his late teens, after sneaking into a local karting track and outpacing seasoned racers with a borrowed kart, that the spark truly ignited. The track owner, impressed by Marcos' raw talent, offered him a chance to compete. His early karting career was a rollercoaster of triumphs and near misses, funded by late nights working alongside his father. A defining moment came when, against all odds, he won the Brazilian National Karting Championship, catching the eye of Havolion Racing. Now, at 22, Marcos is navigating the treacherous waters of single-seater racing with Havolion, his inconsistency a constant battle as he strives to prove he belongs among the racing elite. He aims to show he is more than just a lucky karter.
drivingStyle: Marcos' driving style is a captivating blend of aggression and calculated risk. He attacks corners with a ferocious hunger, often pushing the car beyond its limits, a trait that can lead to spectacular overtakes or costly errors. His tire management is his Achilles heel, frequently burning through rubber in his relentless pursuit of speed. He thrives under pressure, often finding an extra gear when the stakes are highest, but that inconsistency always lingers to haunt him.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles. Isabelle, known for her clinical precision, openly criticizes Marcos' aggressive approach, fueling a heated on-track rivalry.
Their rivalry began after a controversial collision during a crucial race, resulting in both drivers losing valuable championship points. The tension remains palpable whenever they share the track.
Silva is an older, more experienced Brazilian driver whom Marcos sees as an obstacle in his path towards representing the country in F1.

quirks: Always wears the same faded wristband his father gave him before every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba track on repeat in the hour leading up to the race start.
Has a habit of adjusting his helmet strap exactly seven times before entering the car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. You can teach someone to drive fast, but you can't teach them to fight."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian National Karting Championship in 2020, a victory that opened doors and proved he had the talent to compete at a higher level.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out while leading his first single-seater race, costing him a potential victory and shaking his confidence.
